profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a corporate law firm preparing a client-facing board governance memo and appendix for a multinational public company that wants a comparative legal briefing on how national institutional systems relate to female board representation across 38 countries. The matter team is splitting work between the governance/advisory workstream and the comparative research/citations workstream. The immediate context is that the partner wants one integrated package by Thursday for use in a board committee prep call, drawing from an underlying academic study covering 2001-07 but framed for current governance advice. The agenda is to align on who owns the country appendix, what version of the country grid and memo will be used, what counts as the 'legal section' versus broader institutional analysis, and when each item will be considered ready for circulation. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, file ownership, status, and deliverable format for the Thursday package.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Board advisory, securities disclosure, governance benchmarking, client-facing board materials
members.background: Elena advises listed-company boards on governance trends and frequently converts academic and comparative material into concise practical memos for directors and governance committees.
members.private_state: She wants a smooth Thursday delivery with minimal last-minute rewriting, and is trying to protect the partner-facing narrative from becoming too technical or over-footnoted.
hidden_assumptions: The 'board memo' means the polished client-ready narrative plus only the short exhibits that directors will actually read, not the full research backup.
The 'latest country grid' is the working spreadsheet she saw in the governance folder after her edits on Monday, which she assumes is now the default shared source.
The 'legal section' should focus on hard-law and soft-law governance levers tied to board diversity, while cultural and labor-market institutions sit outside that section unless briefly referenced.
An item is 'ready to circulate' when it is substantively stable enough for partner and client review even if cites and formatting are cleaned up afterward.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: Cross-jurisdiction legal research, comparative regulatory frameworks, source validation, research appendices
members.background: Daniel supports transactional and advisory teams by building jurisdictional matrices, validating country-law propositions, and maintaining precedent-quality research files.
members.private_state: He wants the research package to remain reusable and defensible across matters, and is concerned that anything sent upward without complete source hygiene will generate avoidable follow-up.
hidden_assumptions: The 'board memo' includes the research appendix and source notes because partners rely on the package as a complete internal record, even if the client sees only part of it.
The 'latest country grid' refers to the research-master workbook on the knowledge drive updated Tuesday night, which supersedes ad hoc copies in the matter folder.

The 'legal section' naturally includes related institutional mechanisms with legal salience, such as quota regimes, disclosure codes, equality frameworks, and state-supported governance structures, not just black-letter board rules.
An item is 'ready to circulate' only when citations are checked, country entries normalized, and the file can be forwarded without caveats beyond minor stylistic edits.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the 'board memo' needs to go out Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the concise client-ready memo and limited exhibits for the board committee discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the memo together with the full comparative appendix and source notes as one coordinated package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law-firm coordination, 'memo' often loosely refers to the whole deliverable set, so each hears familiar shorthand and assumes the other is using the same packaging convention.

misalignment_points.topic: Which file is the 'latest country grid'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to work off the 'latest country grid' for the 38-country appendix.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to the governance-team spreadsheet in the matter workspace that incorporates her Monday board-facing simplifications and country grouping labels.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is referring to the knowledge team's master workbook on the central drive updated Tuesday with source corrections and restored country-level coding fields.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both files are descendants of the same original matrix, both are plausibly 'latest' from each person's workflow, and neither expects duplicate near-final versions to be in active use.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Daniel will tighten the 'legal section' before Elena folds it into the memo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena uses 'legal section' to mean a narrow portion on regulatory and governance rules directly affecting board composition or disclosure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel uses 'legal section' to mean the broader institutional-law segment, including equality frameworks, code-based governance mechanisms, and legally embedded institutional supports discussed alongside culture.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to using 'legal section' as an internal shorthand, and the underlying study itself blends legal and institutional frameworks in a way that makes the boundary feel obvious to each from their own practice.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They say the appendix should be 'ready to circulate' by end of day Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena thinks this means substantive content is stable enough for partner/client sharing, with cite cleanup and formatting polish still possible overnight.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel thinks this means the appendix is publication-clean internally: citations verified, country labels standardized, and no unresolved source caveats.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same status phrase in competent legal practice, but in advisory versus knowledge workflows the threshold differs subtly; because both are aiming for quality, the phrase sounds fully aligned.
